solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Provoke tumult in high places?

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or tumult
up means aloft, in a high place

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble among the powerful, causing an uproar at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'in high places' is read literally as UP rather than as a phrase about powerful people.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble is to provoke or incite it; the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Set and positioned Greek letter back inside

indicators.note: inside places the turned letter name within the word for positioned

parts.note: positioned means placed, sited

indicators.note: back tells us the Greek letter's name is read in reverse

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T

explanation.surface: A description of placing a Greek letter back where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the definition, though it looks like part of the instructions; 'back' makes UAT, which 'inside' places in the word for positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated is a synonym: something set somewhere is located or placed there.

clue.text: Veggies are meant to be this well done

definitions.text: Veggies are meant to be this
definitions.meaning: vegetables are said to be healthy, beneficial to eat

explanation.surface: A parent praising a child who has finished their vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both healthy, as greens are claimed to be, and an exclamation of praise.

clue.text: Smaller runner runs poorly

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
poorly means sick, ill

explanation.surface: A lesser athlete runs badly in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is not an athlete but something that runs, a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a very small stream, a lesser kind of running water.

clue.text: African seen buffeted by winds close to village

indicators.note: buffeted means knocked about, so the letters of seen are thrown into a new order

parts.note: gales are strong winds

indicators.note: close to means the end, the final letter of village

explanation.surface: An African spotted being blown about by strong winds near a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffeted by' reads as weather acting on the seen person, but only 'buffeted' is the signal, making SENE; 'winds' is a noun here, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegalese is a person from Senegal, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Chat needed about Romeo's apparel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for chat goes round the letter

parts.note: gab is idle chatter
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Discussion is required regarding what Romeo is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GAB around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb means clothing or dress, the same as apparel.

clue.text: Female on moon lifted boring gear

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up
in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a girl is a female
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A woman on the moon raised some drilling equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: GIRL above IO makes GIRLIO; 'lifted' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling platform bores into the seabed for petroleum, so it is drilling equipment.

clue.text: Pitch business — regret showing up Brussels employee?

indicators.note: showing up in a down clue means the letters appear read upwards

parts.note: pitch is tar
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A sales pitch with business regret appearing for an EU official.
explanation.walkthrough: TARCORUE is read upwards by 'showing up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurocrat is an official of the European Union, whose institutions are based in Brussels.

clue.text: Fossil — see black one with dull exterior

indicators.note: with dull exterior means the word for dull forms the outside around the rest

parts.note: trite means dull, hackneyed
lo is an old word meaning look, see
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Look at a black fossil with a dull outer surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' puts TRITE around LOBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods well known from their fossils.

clue.text: Share Jill Masterson's fate? It's goodbye!

parts.note: in the Bond film Goldfinger, Jill Masterson dies covered in gold paint, so sharing her fate is to die in gold

explanation.surface: A Bond fan bidding farewell, hoping not to meet the same end as a Bond girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Dying in gold is DIE wrapped in AU, the chemical symbol for gold, so the first part is a cryptic picture of the letters rather than a mechanism the parser can name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, used in English to mean goodbye.

clue.text: Old rune reworked as circular device

indicators.note: reworked means made over, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An ancient runic character has been redesigned as a round emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' rearranges the letters of OLD RUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a circular emblem, such as the RAF's ring marking on aircraft.

clue.text: Neo backing British stars in trade restriction

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: Neo is this puzzle's setter, who would call themself me
Argo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: The setter supports British celebrities caught up in a trade ban.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Neo is ME; 'backing' turns it to EM. Argo (Argo Navis) is an old southern constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a particular country.

clue.text: Amount in kitty put in pocket

definitions.meaning: the total money staked in a game or pool
in snooker or pool, to sink a ball into a pocket

explanation.surface: Pocketing the money in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the pool of money in a game and, as a verb, to sink a ball in snooker.

clue.text: Performer seen in shop erasing errors

indicators.note: seen in signals the letters can be found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A performer is spotted in a shop correcting mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' points to the letters running through 'shop erasing errors'.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano or tenor in opera is one kind of musical performer.

clue.text: Universal anagram came in clue

indicators.note: the word anagram itself declares that the letters which follow are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter boasting that a universal anagram turned up in a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' rearranges CAME IN CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical means general or worldwide in scope, especially across the whole Christian church.

clue.text: Bride at Savoy announcing herself in agitation?

parts.note: someone introducing herself says 'I'm', giving IM
Patience, the milkmaid heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera of that name, first staged at the Savoy Theatre, ends up married

explanation.surface: A bride at the Savoy hotel introduces herself in a nervous state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy here is the London theatre that staged Gilbert and Sullivan operas; one is Patience. Her introduction, 'I'm Patience', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is restless eagerness, a kind of agitation; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: Friend has bishop purchase round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for purchase goes round the bishop

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by a bishop

explanation.surface: A friend has a bishop buy a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests a round of drinks but means surrounding. A bishop is typically a Doctor of Divinity, hence DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy is an informal word for a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Bad suggestion must be unsettling monarch

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Poor advice that is bound to disturb the ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' rearranges MUST BE to BUMST; ER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum steer is slang for misleading advice or false information.

clue.text: American and English in exploit

explanation.surface: Americans and English involved in some daring deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploit' looks like a noun, a feat, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Ornament ancient Briton carries round

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the word for the ancient Briton holds the round letter

parts.note: the Picts were ancient people of northern Britain
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton bearing a circular decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts O inside PICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop in lace or embroidery edging, a type of trim.

clue.text: Prompt monster to report mathematical value

indicators.note: to report means to say out loud, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: a prompt is a cue and a monster a brute, giving 'cue brute'

explanation.surface: Urging a beast to report a mathematical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to report' signals that 'cue brute' spoken aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube root is the number that, multiplied by itself three times, gives a given number.

clue.text: Evaluation made by certain people in essence

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these words go into the word for essence

parts.note: the meat of something is its essence or substance
sure means certain
men are people

explanation.surface: An assessment made by confident people in essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in essence' looks like a stock phrase meaning basically; here 'in' is the containment signal and 'essence' is the meat of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Measurement is the act of gauging size or amount, a form of assessment.

clue.text: Manual rewritten for female graduate

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handbook revised for a woman who has graduated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges MANUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumna is the feminine Latin form for a former student of a school or college.

clue.text: Sound like hounds or one among horses

definitions.meaning: to howl or bark deeply as hunting dogs do
a reddish-brown horse is one kind of horse

explanation.surface: Something that howls like a dog or is part of a herd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hound's deep howl and also a reddish-brown horse with black points.

clue.text: Nodding acquaintances?

parts.note: the phrase normally means people known slightly; here it is read literally as associates who always nod in agreement

explanation.surface: People one knows only well enough to nod to.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who agree with everything a boss says are always nodding, so they are literally nodding associates.

clue.text: Wave from our setter on time to meet French friend

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means coming after the next piece

parts.note: the sun is what sets in our sky each evening
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: The setter waves on time to greet a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our setter' looks like the puzzle's setter, but means the thing that sets: the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake or underwater disturbance.

clue.text: Singer trapped in chemical toilet

indicators.note: trapped in signals the letters are caught inside the following words

explanation.surface: A vocalist is stuck in a portable toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' points to the letters spanning 'chemical toilet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Mad Hatter beginning to suspect cultural world

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
beginning to means the first letter of suspect

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice is starting to suspect high culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HATTER; 'beginning to' adds S, the first letter of suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, music, theatre and literature together make up a society's cultural world.

clue.text: Cheers: cheers and cheerio

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, as is cheers
again ta, an informal word for thanks

explanation.surface: Three ways of saying cheers, as a casual farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'cheers' and 'ta' both mean thanks, while 'cheerio' means goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, as cheerio is.

clue.text: Bear — one sits regularly for surrealist

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A bear sitting down at regular times for a surrealist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and every other letter of 'Bear one sits'. Max Ernst was a German surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German artist and a leading figure of Dada and Surrealism.

clue.text: Take choir out to Jerusalem?

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a choir out to perform in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerusalem' looks like the city, but the Jerusalem artichoke is a root vegetable; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerusalem artichoke is a knobbly tuber, one variety named with that word.
